Theme

Work & responsibility

agenda noun

also the agenda, on the agenda, what’s on the agenda, to-do list, order of business, item on the agenda

classical

Vives, Exercitātiō 20: is praescrībit aliīs quae sint agenda

quae agenda sunt

relative clause with the gerundive of agō; the tense of esse and the mood follow the sentence

what is to be done: the business in hand

Latin says what has to be done rather than naming a list: Quae hodiē agenda sunt?, what’s on today? The neuter plural agenda is the gerundive, the source of the English word, and is used as a noun only in later Latin.

Other words

  • rērum agendārum index — a written agenda, a list of business

    noun phrase: index, indicis m. · also used · modern · Levi–Bini p. 44, s.v. ordine del giorno

    For the paper itself. Classically index is a list or table of contents (Quint. 10.1.57; Lewis & Short).

  • relātiō, relātiōnis f. — a motion or item laid before a meeting

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Pis. 29: nōn modo āctiōnem aliquam aut relātiōnem (Lewis & Short); Levi–Bini p. 44, s.v. ordine del giorno

    The matter a presiding magistrate put to the senate (referre ad senātum): an item on a formal agenda, not a list of chores.

Examples

  • Quae hodiē agenda sunt?

    What’s on the agenda today?composed

  • lūdēmus lūdum, in quō ūnus ēligitur rēx; is praescrībit aliīs quae sint agenda

    we’ll play the game where one of us is chosen king; he tells the others what is to be doneVives, Exercitātiō 20

See also plan, meeting, list.
